svg.title: Table Partitioning
svg.desc: Table Partitioning. Split a large table into partitions by range, list or hash, so queries skip partitions and old data is dropped in an instant. Step 1, One table, slow cleanup: A week's report reads all 11,030 pages; deleting old months leaves dead rows and 87 MB of WAL. Step 2, Partition by month: Each month becomes a table of its own with its own indexes, and every row is routed by happened_at. Step 3, Pruning and retention: The week now reads 2 of 25 partitions, and retention detaches and drops 10 old months in 38 ms. Step 4, Keys, plans and limits: Unique keys must include happened_at, queries without it search every partition, all on one server.

g.text: A week's report reads all 11,030 pages; deleting old months leaves dead rows and 87 MB of WAL.
Each month becomes a table of its own with its own indexes, and every row is routed by happened_at.
The week now reads 2 of 25 partitions, and retention detaches and drops 10 old months in 38 ms.
Unique keys must include happened_at, queries without it search every partition, all on one server.
SELECT count(*) FROM order_events WHERE happened_at >= '2026-08-31' AND happened_at < '2026-09-07'
CREATE TABLE order_events (…) PARTITION BY RANGE (happened_at)
INSERT INTO order_events OVERRIDING SYSTEM VALUE SELECT * FROM order_events_old
ALTER TABLE order_events DETACH PARTITION order_events_2024_12 CONCURRENTLY
CREATE TABLE order_events (id bigint PRIMARY KEY, …) PARTITION BY RANGE (happened_at)
Parallel Seq Scan: all 11,030 pages read, 1,483,592 rows filtered out
4,703 empty pages, still in the file

g.text: INSERT into the parent: PostgreSQL routes each row to the partition whose range holds its happened_at
the other 23 partitions were pruned while planning: they are not in the plan at all
the 10 months before October 2025: detached, then dropped; 639,726 rows and 67 MB gone at once
no happened_at in the WHERE clause, so nothing is pruned: all 15 partitions are searched
id bigint GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY,
order_id bigint NOT NULL REFERENCES orders (id),
kind text NOT NULL, happened_at timestamptz NOT NULL,
PRIMARY KEY (id, happened_at) -- must include the key
CREATE TABLE order_events_2026_09 PARTITION OF order_events
· an ordinary table of its own
its own indexes, created from the parent’s:
a partition created later gets both indexes automatically
one run, during a 3 s query
DROP TABLE of a partition → ACCESS EXCLUSIVE on order_events: the next report queued behind it for 2.04 s
DETACH … CONCURRENTLY → SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE: the same report ran in 0.05 s
the foreign key to orders still locks orders to detach and to drop: run retention with a short lock_timeout
→ 12 more Index Scans, 2 Seq Scans of empty ones
Unique keys must include the key
a PRIMARY KEY on id alone fails:
so the key is (id, happened_at), and no
index checks that id alone is unique
planning a query that can’t prune (median of 7)
first run in a new session: 23 ms; 1,107 locks
docs: fine up to a few thousand if queries prune
all 15 partitions share one server’s CPU,
memory, disk and WAL; spreading the rows
the same rule for unique keys, and no foreign
keys at all on partitioned InnoDB tables
